36.02505,-79.36509: John Butler. Orange County sheriff in War of Regulation, 1770-1771; brigadier general, N.C. militia, 1777-84. Lived ¼ mi. N.
36.06042,-79.43351: Pyle's Defeat. Tory militia going to join Cornwallis's army destroyed by Lee's Legion Feb. 1781 nearby on Col. Michael Holt's land.
36.06532,-79.40053: Graham College. Est. by the Christian Church, 1851, as Graham Institute; forerunner of Elon College. Burned in 1892. Stood 1 blk. west.
36.07164,-79.09932: Occaneechi. Village of Occaneechi Indians on the Great Trading Path. Inhabited ca. 1680-1710. Visited in 1701 by the explorer John Lawson. 1/2 mi. E.
36.07177,-79.09931: William Churton. Cartographer. Surveyed Granville District. In 1749 extended N.C.-Va. boundary line 90 miles west. Lived nearby.
36.07392,-79.09938: James Hogg 1729 1804. Merchant. Left native Scotland, 1774. Partner in Transylvania Company; UNC trustee. Home 1/2 mi. E.; grave 2 blks. N.
36.07421,-79.09939: Billy Strayhorn 1915 1967. Jazz composer & pianist. Wrote "Take the A Train" and other songs for Duke Ellington Orchestra. Boyhood home site 1/4 mi. W.
North Carolina Society Of The Cincinnati. Formed Oct. 23, 1783, in Hillsborough, by officers of the Continental Line. First President was General Jethro Sumner.
36.0747,-79.09941: Edmund Fanning 1776 1847. Judge and local official. Target of Regulators who ransacked and destroyed his nearby home, 1770.
36.0748,-79.09941: Regulators Hanged. After the Regulators were defeated at Alamance, May 16, 1771, six of their number were hanged, 1/4 mile east, June 19, 1771.
36.07517,-79.09943: Thomas Burke. Governor of N.C., was captured in Hillsboro by David Fanning and his Tories, Sept. 12, 1781, and taken to Charleston, S.C.
36.07671,-79.09952: Moses A. Curtis. Botanist, authority on North American flora, author, and Episcopal minister. Home was two blocks east.
36.0769,-79.09952: J. G. De Roulhac Hamilton. Historian, professor, & founder of the Southern Historical Collection at UNC. Born 1/2 block W.
36.07699,-79.09954: Thomas Ruffin 1787 1870. Jurist and agriculturist. Chief Justice of North Carolina Supreme Court, 1833-1852 and 1858-1859. Grave 3/10 mile east.
36.07723,-79.09948: Francis Nash. Patriot general in American Revolution, was mortally wounded at Germantown, 1777. His home is 150 yds. W.
36.07737,-79.09948: William A. Graham. Governor, 1845-1849; Secretary of the Navy; United States Senator; Whig nominee for Vice-President in 1852. His home stands 150 yds. W.
36.07756,-79.09949: William Hooper 1742 1790. One of North Carolina's three signers of the Declaration of Independence. His home is 150 yds. W. Was buried a few yds. W.
36.07847,-79.09954: Constitutional Convention, 1788. Delegates debated U.S. Constitution, July 21-Aug. 4, 1788, & voted to delay ratification until bill of rights was added. Met 100 yards S.W.
36.0801,-79.09961: Elizabeth Keckly Ca. 1820 1907. Burwell family slave, bought freedom, 1855. Dressmaker & friend to Mary Todd Lincoln. Published her memoir, 1868. Lived here, 1830s.
36.08331,-79.14189: Hart's Mill. Grist mill. Site of key Regulator meeting, 1766, and skirmish in 1781 that boosted the Patriot cause. Stood 1/5 mile N.
36.09412,-79.43704: North Carolina Railroad. Company Shops built here in 1857 for maintenance and repair of the N.C. Railroad. Closed in 1866.
36.09723,-79.41425: J. Spencer Love 1896 1962. Founder of Burlington Mills, 1924; success of rayon propelled world's largest textile company. "Pioneer Plant" 3/4 mi. S.
